newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gulf Air drops Geneva route to New York - official.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air drops Geneva route to New York - official.

text.p: Gulf Air, the airline operated by four Arab states in the Gulf, is to stop flying its new route to New York through Geneva, the Swiss city's Cointrin international airport management reported on Thursday.
In a press statement, airport officials said the service, started at the end of last October and flown three times a week, would be halted from February 15.

Gulf Air -- owned by Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Qatar -- launched the route as an extension of a twice-weekly service from the Gulf to Geneva in the hope it would win local passenger pick-up rights for the New York leg.

But Swiss government officials in Berne, whom Geneva authorities accuse of favouring Zurich's Kloten airport, have so far refused to grant extended pick-up rights, allowing Gulf Air only to take on passengers changing flights in Cointrin.

"With these restrictions, it was impossible to market the route and the management of Gulf Air, in view of the airline's financial situation, could not maintain the service," the Geneva airport statement said.
Gulf Air announced earlier this month that it was in financial difficulties and would have to sell six of its Boeing 767 airliners and drop several international routes.
